finding: The prior released build already supports deep publication for a small interactive offline render.
probe: Factory cube, CPU, 32x32, 4 samples, normal non-background Blender, bpy.ops.render.render(INVOKE_DEFAULT), the operator invoked by F12.
architecture: Cycles background means offline (also F12); BlenderSession.headless reflects bpy.app.background. F12 uses the same BlenderOutputDriver as background final renders. Viewport has background=false; baking has a separate driver setup.
feasibility: No separate deep driver appears necessary. Retaining interactive capture in the new layer-based adapter would require revising the requested CLI-only headless guards and warning policy after user approval.
risks: The small existing-build probe does not qualify large scenes, GPU backends, cancellation, repeated renders or animation in the UI.
Deep export can delay interactive completion; cancellation must preserve the prior final EXR and release capture/spill resources.
Large diagnostic sidecars should remain opt-in.
Final render, preview, viewport and baking must remain distinct; the optional null layer keeps the latter callers deep-off.
Display-driver/context lifetime and repeated/persistent sessions need interactive regression coverage.
draft_behavior: Implements the agreed warning and no deep file for F12, which intentionally restricts functionality observed in the prior build.
